findings.title: Grading abandons the benchmark-wide spend contract
findings.description: Architecture 420 requires one benchmark cap covering replay, grading and judging. D9 explicitly replaces it with independent invocation caps. Moreover, its “at most $15.18” claim is unsupported: the overshoot figure is an observed estimate, not an enforced per-review limit. Preserve benchmark-wide accounting and distinguish estimated spend from an enforceable upper bound.

findings.title: Report grouping contradicts the consumed config identity
findings.description: D13 groups by `(alias, model, profile, effort_sent)`, contradicting this document’s prerequisite at line 58 and slice 420 D6. The required identity excludes aliases and includes `tool_use` and `max_output_tokens`. The proposed grouping can split identical configurations or merge different ones, invalidating paired comparisons. Use the required wire-level identity consistently.

findings.title: Newly skipped regressions can receive a passing grade
findings.description: D2 assumes skipped and xfailed nodes have the same outcome at the start commit, but D8 records only baseline node ids and snapshots—not baseline test outcomes. Producer source or dependency changes can cause formerly passing tests to skip or xfail. Accepting those outcomes unconditionally undermines the architecture’s producer-independent regression grade. Record baseline outcomes and define how newly skipped or xfailed nodes affect the grade.

findings.title: Reviewer rules are neither reliably pinned nor consistently identified
findings.description: The review runs after applying the producer diff and loads rules from that sandbox, while calling them “the start commit’s.” No step restores or independently reads historical rules. A producer can therefore change the grading instructions. Additionally, D10 defines one grader identity for the benchmark although cases can have different historical rules hashes. Load rules explicitly from each case’s start commit and represent their identity consistently in grade lookup and comparison.

findings.title: Reviewer timeout handling does not specify termination
findings.description: `asyncio.wait_for` specifies cancellation, but the design does not state how an active provider request or reviewer subprocess is terminated and reaped before sandbox removal. This leaves the new review I/O path’s timeout handling incomplete: work could continue spending or accessing a deleted tree. Define cancellation propagation, bounded teardown and accounting for interrupted calls.

findings.title: Recall integration introduces a forbidden sequencing dependency
findings.description: The slice plan explicitly permits 427 to be built independently after 421. This design instead requires 427 to import reviewer and bootstrap utilities introduced by 425. Preserve that independence by placing genuinely shared contracts below both slices, or have 425 consume 427’s recall interface without making 427 depend on grading.

Report grouping contradicts the consumed config identity

Reviewer rules are neither reliably pinned nor consistently identified
Reviewer timeout handling does not specify termination
